facts:
## CELL FACTS

Cell 木_正官 (Wood carrying The Magistrate). Persona The Magistrate (正官). Definition line: "Framework-mediated pressure, the standard that steadies". Keyword Order, charge gentle, poles catalyst Integrity / friction Rigidity. Family function: Order. Cost dimension: the standard that steadies; the frame that holds you holds you in. Arena: the gate, the seal, order, the appointed hour. Classical portrait: framework-mediated pressure; the standard that steadies; rank held by rules, rigidity as the shadow. Ruled domains: Career, Status, Order. Sibling (other polarity of the family): 七杀.
Element arena: Wood (trunk, branch, root, grain, growth, the forest). dm_element (which core reads this cell): Earth. structural_interaction seed: "Wood setting standard for Earth cross-polarity — movement asking whether stability is living".
- k2_overview: "Your Wood moves as the Magistrate: living order that grows. You build careers and codes like trellises, principled frames that help everything on them climb. Authority suits you when it nurtures. People accept your rules because your rules have leaves. Prune the dead ones each season and the frame stays believed in."
- k2_functional: "Order is your native climate: you grow straight inside good structure and warp without it."
- adj_chips: {"catalyst":["Straight-growing","Honorable","Leads by example"],"friction":"[REDACTED: the words under test]"}
- k2_domain_readings: {"Career":"Your career grows like a managed forest: steady rings, widening responsibility, roots deepening in one good house. Choose organizations you would plant a decade in. Transplanting yearly wastes your kind of compounding.","Status":"Your standing grows organically: respect accruing ring by ring until you are somehow the oak everyone consults. Let it. Just keep lower branches reachable.","Order":"Your order is cultivated: rules as trellises rather than cages, standards that make growing easier. Systems you design get adopted willingly. Revisit them each season so the living thing never outgrows the frame."}
- fn_reading.friction.ledger (three rows, index-aligned to adj_chips.friction; authored order is significance order):
  - row 0: [REDACTED: the target row]
  - row 1: [REDACTED: the target row]
  - row 2: [REDACTED: the target row]
- Sibling cell 木_七杀 chips (nothing you write may fit the sibling): {"catalyst":["Hard-trained","Focused","Storm-tested"],"friction":["Severe","Straining","Overdriven"]}
- Sibling cell 木_七杀 friction row 0 drive passage, for the sibling test on the tension (this row must name a different either-or): "Your standards fall on people like frost, necessary in your mind, killing in effect. The praise is rare, the corrections are exact, and small errors get treated as character evidence. You are hardest on yourself, which is true, and which warms nobody."

Core element Earth, energy element Wood. Law: Wood tames Earth (木克土: roots hold the hillside). Relative to the core the energy is the tamer, so Wood is this core's Order. No chart is attached to this batch: the cell is written for every chart with a Earth core that shows Wood on the friction pole, so no percentage and no state of one chart appears in any value. The friction pole of Wood as the Order is the Underfueled band's case (the core burns more than it takes in); tone by pole: reminder. Rows: row 0, row 1, row 2, each with its three angles (drive, cost_self, cost_others: the drive, the cost to the reader, the cost to others; the app shows one angle per row by position rotation, so each passage must stand alone); one chip per row, written once and copied byte-identical onto the row's three fields. The pair cell 土_木's definition and advice for this pole are rewritten in the same batch (the pair skeleton) and are withheld here; no four-word run may be shared with them, so keep every phrase the ledger's own.

value.text: You go by the book, even where it was never meant to reach. Wood presses on a core with little spare, so you trust the written rule rather than your own judgment. Remember that you go to the book for safety first and sense second.

value_b.text: Going by the book is the only fairness you trust. Because the written rule asks nothing of your nerve, you apply it to the letter instead of to the case. It is worth remembering that you serve the case, and the book only helps.

value.text: You never bend, whatever the day asks. Wood holds you upright past the point of use, so you brace against a change of plan rather than lean into it. Bear in mind that bending is not the same as breaking.

value_b.text: Bending feels to you like losing, so you never do it. Wood puts more pressure on you than your core wants, and holding stiff is how you carry it. Keep in mind that you would sooner break than bend, and only bending heals.

value.text: Rank comes first with you, yours and everyone else's. Because a clear ladder tells you where you stand, you check who is higher up ahead of who is right. Know that you want the order more than the answer, and the job needs the answer.

value_b.text: You put rank first, ahead of the person holding it. Wood sets a frame on you that your core does not fill, so you cling to the order of things. Notice that you see the rank and forget to look at the face.

value.text: In how you treat people, rank comes first, whether you mean it or not. Since order feels safer than equals, you give the person above you your best ahead of the one beside you. You leave the one beside you whatever is left.
